final_briefs.title: rustyfiles
final_briefs.description: **rustyfiles delivers a fast, never‑freezing file manager for Windows and macOS, built in Rust.** It offers tabs, dual panes, archive‑as‑folder support and Quick‑Look‑style previews. The README shows a folder of 100 000 files opening in 281 ms, and the project ships binaries for Windows 11 (x64 | ARM64) and macOS 26 on Apple silicon (beta).
final_briefs.why_it_matters: A Rust‑written file manager that stays responsive even with massive directories, showing how systems‑level Rust can replace native Explorer/Finder for power users.
final_briefs.who_cares: Desktop application developers, Rust enthusiasts, and power users who need a fast, reliable file manager on Windows or macOS.

final_briefs.title: AI made self‑hosting fun again
final_briefs.description: **AI coding assistants are lowering the friction of tweaking Docker‑Compose and scripts, reigniting enthusiasm for self‑hosting.** The author keeps infrastructure as code in Git (Docker Compose files, scripts) and now lets AI agents edit configurations, add services, or automate tasks, turning ideas that once required an evening of reading changelogs into quick, executable changes.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Shows how AI coding assistants can cut the friction of tweaking Docker‑Compose, scripts, and other infra code, reigniting enthusiasm for self‑hosting.
final_briefs.who_cares: DevOps engineers, SREs, hobbyist sysadmins, and anyone maintaining self‑hosted services.

final_briefs.title: Fix: Claude Code 'Couldn't Share Transcript' 403 Error
final_briefs.description: **A practical workaround shows that a persistent 403 when sharing transcripts in Claude Code is an account‑side issue, not a local bug.** The suggested steps are to re‑run `/login` to confirm a fresh session; if the 403 remains, treat it as an Anthropic account/permission problem and copy the transcript manually as a temporary solution.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete workaround for a 403 error when sharing transcripts in Claude Code, saving time for developers relying on Anthropic’s CLI.
final_briefs.who_cares: Developers using Claude Code or other Anthropic tools in their workflow.

final_briefs.title: OCR vs. ICR: A Developer's Guide to Passport Data Extraction
final_briefs.description: **Understanding the difference between OCR and ICR helps you choose the right engine for passport data extraction in onboarding pipelines.** OCR converts printed text (including the MRZ) into machine‑readable characters, while ICR is designed for handwriting and more variable styles. The guide walks through the typical OCR workflow—capture, preprocess, recognize, structure—and explains where ICR might be needed.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Clarifies the trade‑offs between OCR and ICR for passport data extraction, guiding engineers to pick the right technology for identity‑verification pipelines.
final_briefs.who_cares: Engineers building digital onboarding, KYC, or any document‑processing system that must read passports or similar IDs.
